To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyclic amino acid spin-label 2,2, 6,6-Tetrnethylpiperidine-l-oxyl- 4-amino- 4-carboxyic acid (TOAC) can be incorporated into a peptide by solid phase peptide synthesis and used to study the dynamics of a peptide-protein complex by paramagnetic N M R.
the TOAC spin-label is a useful paramagnetic NMR probe for studies of protein-protein interactions.

the binding affinity of a proline-rich Src SH3 binding peptide is reduced substantially when a cyclic, rigid spin-label is incorporated within the binding motif, whereas the binding constant remains almost unaffected when the spin-label is placed just outside the motif.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of NMR spectroscopy to investigate the structure and function of proteins, in particular the structure of protein complexes and their dynamics.
the development and application of paramagnetic NMR techniques for studying protein-protein interactions.
the application of paramagnetic NMR to the study of protein-protein complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of the peptide to the Src SH-3 domain is weak but specific and that the binding of TOAC to Src SH-3 is weaker than that of the unmodified FAK peptide.
TOAC can indeed be used for NMR structural investigations of protein-ligand complexes, but that the results should always be interpreted with caution.

the TOAC spin-label is useful for studying protein-protein interactions, but that the binding affinity of the spin-labelled peptides is reduced, and that the TOAC side-chain is not a very good reporter for the dynamics of the protein complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
paramagnetic NMR is a useful tool to study the interaction of SH3 domains with peptides.
TOAC is a useful tool for paramagnetic NMR studies.
TOAC can provide a reliable paramagnetic Nmr restraint for studying the dynamics of a protein-protein interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TOAC label is a useful tool for studying protein-peptide interactions, provided that the label is positioned outside the binding motif of a peptide.
the use of a rigid spin label is not detrimental in itself.
TOAC can serve as a general tool for studying the interaction of peptides and proteins by NMR.
